extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for Senior Area Chairs overseeing Area Chairs and the peer-review process for NeurIPS 2025, including operational responsibilities, timelines, conflict-of-interest and confidentiality rules, and decision calibration with program chairs. The document tells SACs what to monitor, intervene on, and how to interact with ACs, reviewers, authors, and PCs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oversee ACs and ensure reviewing process runs smoothly
rubrics_metrics.description: As an SAC, your role is to oversee the work of a small number of ACs, making sure that the reviewing process goes smoothly. SACs serve as the first point of contact for ACs if they need assistance or guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Help ACs chase late reviewers, calibrate decisions across ACs, and discuss borderline papers. During final decision-making, discuss all proposed decisions with the program chairs (PCs). If an AC is unresponsive you will need to step in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure papers have at least three high-quality reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that all papers have at least 3 quality reviews by the reviewing deadline and before the author response period starts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACs should ensure reviewers have completed reviews; send reminder emails if needed; read all reviews to ensure they are up to standards. If reviewers are missing or reviews are low quality, find emergency reviewers or otherwise remedy the situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check review content for respectful and appropriate language
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure that ACs check for any disrespectful or derogatory language in the reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You are ultimately responsible for ensuring reviews are high quality and respectful; intervene if you find derogatory or disrespectful content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiate and monitor reviewer-author discussions during author response period
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure ACs initiate reviewer-author discussions as soon as the author response is entered and that reviewers engage in the discussion phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assigned ACs have not initiated discussions, prompt them to do so. Phase 1 (Thur, Jul 31 – Wed, Aug 6) is primarily for reviewers to engage with authors before closed reviewer/AC discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oversee AC-reviewer discussions (phase 2) to ensure active engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: During the second discussion phase, ensure reviewers interact with the AC and among themselves and that there is active engagement, especially for papers with conflicting reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for active engagement on papers where there are positive and negative reviews; prompt further discussion where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remind ACs to submit preliminary meta-reviews by deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Remind ACs to submit preliminary meta-reviews for each paper by the metareviews deadline and begin scheduling one-on-one discussions with them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider organizing meetings between ACs to help them talk over decisions and better calibrate; you may be present or ask ACs to meet prior to discussing papers with you. Check carefully for COIs before asking ACs to discuss papers with each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read all reviews and meta-reviews and ensure meta-reviews explain decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Read all meta-reviews and ensure they explain paper decisions to the authors and augment the reviews, explaining how reviews, author responses, and discussion were used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dismissing or ignoring a review is not acceptable unless there is a good reason for doing so. If an AC needs guidance, read all reviews for papers assigned to them and make sure they are respectful and acknowledge the authors' response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrate decisions and handle borderline / conflicting cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Help calibrate decisions by working closely with ACs, scheduling meetings with them, and paying particular attention to borderline papers and papers where the AC recommendation conflicts with reviewers' recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may schedule individual or group meetings; be prepared to discuss such cases with program chairs during SAC-PC discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participate in SAC-AC and SAC-PC discussions and finalize decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: SACs discuss papers with ACs and make initial accept/reject decisions (SAC-AC phase) and then meet with program chairs to finalize decisions (SAC-PC phase).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to discuss all borderline papers and cases in which the AC recommendation goes against reviewer recommendations. Update meta-reviews to accurately reflect the final decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be responsive and respect deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Respond to emails and communications promptly and respect deadlines; inform program chairs if you will be unavailable for more than a few days during important windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your preferred email in OpenReview is accurate and that emails from noreply@openreview.net don't go to spam. If unavailable (e.g., vacation) during key windows, notify PCs as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be proactive in managing ACs and reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactively check that ACs are responsive, help them find emergency reviewers, and make sure discussions are happening on their papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is your responsibility to ensure the review process goes smoothly; check in on AC responsiveness and follow up as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be kind and accomodating of personal circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge that personal situations may lead to late or unfinished work among reviewers and ACs; exercise empathy and understanding in communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reviewer or AC cannot complete work on time, be considerate and possibly pick up slack. Make back-up plans with another reviewer or AC and be flexible to the extent possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect and enforce conflict-of-interest rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Be on the lookout for uncaught conflicts of interest, and contact program chairs immediately if you notice any. Do not discuss submissions assigned to your ACs with other SACs without PC approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not talk to other SACs or ACs about submissions you are an author on or submissions with which you have a conflict of interest. Familiarize yourself with what constitutes conflict of interest for NeurIPS 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality of submissions and review materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep everything relating to the review process confidential and do not use ideas, code, or results from submissions in your own work until they are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not talk about or distribute submissions (code, ideas, results) to anyone without prior approval from program chairs. Code submitted for reviewing cannot be distributed. If inviting external reviewers, do so through OpenReview rather than sharing submissions through another channel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow NeurIPS code of conduct and related reviewer/AC guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Read and agree to abide by the NeurIPS code of conduct and familiarize yourself with the AC guidelines and Reviewer guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will interact significantly with ACs, so ensure you understand what is expected of them and be consistent with NeurIPS policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep OpenReview profile and contact information up to date
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure your preferred email address and OpenReview profile are accurate so you receive assignments and important emails.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emails come from noreply@openreview.net and may be marked as spam; check your spam folder and whitelist that address if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use official channels for support and conflict questions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you encounter an unresolved situation, contact the program chairs at pc2025@neurips.cc; for OpenReview issues, email info@openreview.net.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact program chairs for COI questions and other escalations. Do not attempt to resolve certain issues unilaterally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage emergency reviewing and recruitment of additional reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Be prepared to get additional/emergency reviewers during the emergency reviewing window if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SACs will be informed when the process for inviting emergency reviewers is available; help ACs find emergency reviewers and coordinate emergency reviewing windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check AC assignments and raise concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: When you receive your assignment (about ~10 ACs), review it carefully and email the program chairs if you have any concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you are comfortable with the ACs assigned to you and their load; raise issues early.
